paragraphs.source_en: Nobuyasu had been a dear child, unbearably difficult to forsake. Ieyasu, too, had felt it a terrible waste, more than he could endure. Yet unending warfare would mercilessly spread the tragedy of Nobuyasu and Ieyasu across all Japan. It was this thought that allowed reason to prevail over emotion. But did Mitsuhide yearn as fiercely as Ieyasu did for an end to war?
